## U.S. Government and Tech Giants Drive Innovation in Key Sectors; New Leveraged ETFs Emerge

The latter half of 2026 has seen significant activity from U.S. government entities, defense organizations, and leading technology companies in the quantum tech, drone tech, robotics, space tech, satellite communication, nuclear energy, and artificial intelligence (AI) sectors. Concurrently, new single-stock 2x leveraged ETFs are set to launch, offering investors direct exposure to the daily performance of emerging tech giants.

### Government Initiatives Fueling Advanced Technologies

**Nuclear Energy**
The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) has demonstrated a strong commitment to expanding domestic nuclear generation. The DOE announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $17.5 billion to support the deployment of 10 new large-scale nuclear reactors across as many as five project sites in the United States. Further strengthening the sector, the DOE also issued conditional loan commitments of up to $5 billion to Constellation Energy and up to $4.2 billion to Vistra for nuclear uprates and modernization across their fleets in Illinois, Maryland, Pennsylvania, and Ohio, respectively. These efforts aim to add nearly 1.1 gigawatts (GW) and 433 megawatts (MW) of electricity, respectively, to the grid and enhance national energy security.

**Robotics and AI**
The DOE is investing in advanced robotics and AI for scientific discovery. It selected four national-laboratory-led projects (from Argonne, Brookhaven, Oak Ridge, and SLAC) to develop robotics and automation testbeds with a total funding of $30 million, including $2 million in fiscal year 2026. These projects will focus on developing reusable software, robot skills, and digital-twin environments. Additionally, the DOE's $320 million "Genesis Mission," launched in November 2025, aims to build a shared AI-powered research platform integrating supercomputers, experimental facilities, and AI systems for accelerated scientific discovery, encompassing robotics and autonomous laboratories. NASA is also leveraging AI, partnering with IBM Research and academic institutions to develop the NASA-IBM Lunar Foundation Model. This AI system, trained on nearly two decades of lunar orbiter data, will help researchers quickly identify features on the moon's surface, including potential landing sites and areas for water ice. NASA's Office of the Chief Science Data Officer is researching "super intelligence" (SI) to enhance the use of its science data, including foundation models and large language models.

**Space Tech and Satellite Communication**
NASA's Space Technology Mission Directorate (STMD) has chosen 41 proposals from 37 companies for "no exchange of funds" collaborations to advance technologies crucial for Moon and Mars missions. These partnerships will mature technologies for space transportation, planetary surface operations, and lunar surface infrastructure. Notable selections include Lockheed Martin, which will advance a modular energy solution for the Moon and a wireless power transfer system, and Kall Morris Inc., developing an Asteria payload attachment system. Blue Origin is working on a "Space-to-Surface Deceleration Capabilities Assessment" and Starcloud on "Flight Demonstration of High-Performance Computing for In-Orbit Autonomy and Exploration" as part of these collaborations.

In satellite communication, the U.S. Space Force has awarded significant contracts. Boeing received a $2 billion deal to build two additional satellites for the Mobile User Objective System (MUOS) Service Life Extension program, ensuring the constellation remains operational through the mid-2030s. Viasat and Intelsat General Communications secured a $437.66 million contract for the Protected Tactical Satellite-Global (PTS-G) program, aimed at procuring jam-resistant military communication satellites. The Space Force also awarded Sphinx Defense a $287 million contract to develop a mission planning prototype for the Evolved Strategic Satellite Communications (ESS) program. The U.S. Marine Corps awarded Viasat's Inmarsat Government business a $307.1 million contract for global satellite communication connectivity under the MECS2 program.

**Innovative Technologies**
Across the U.S. government, programs like SBIR and STTR continue to provide over $4 billion annually to small businesses for innovation and research and development across various agencies including NIH, DoD, and NSF. The National Science Foundation's (NSF) Technology, Innovation, and Partnerships (TIP) directorate is actively working to accelerate the advancement of key technologies, particularly in AI, Quantum Information Science and Technology (QIST), and biotechnology. The CHIPS and Science Act authorizes $11 billion for R&D in semiconductor manufacturing.

### "Magnificent 7" Companies and Prominent Investor Activities

**Artificial Intelligence (AI)**
Meta Platforms has significantly increased its bet on artificial intelligence, raising its 2026 capital expenditure outlook to between $135 billion and $145 billion. To support this, Meta announced a new class of nonvoting Class C stock, expected to begin trading in January 2027, to fund infrastructure and acquisitions for its AI initiatives. Meta's AI agent, Muse, has garnered over 10 million users in the U.S. and Canada within six weeks and is now entering a scaling phase, with expectations to improve cost efficiency and achieve profitability.

Apple has been active in AI through strategic acquisitions. In January 2026, Apple acquired the Israeli AI startup Q.ai for a reported price nearing $2 billion. Q.ai specializes in interpreting whispered speech and enhancing audio in noisy environments, with potential applications for AirPods and the Vision Pro headset. Apple is also reportedly seeking to acquire other AI chip companies to reduce its reliance on Nvidia for demanding AI workloads. Its most recent acquisition in October 2026 was Samplab, a Zurich-based developer of AI-powered audio software.

**Satellite Communication and Space Tech**
Amazon's satellite internet constellation, Amazon Leo (formerly Project Kuiper), is on track to begin initial service in "mid-2026" or "this year" (2026), having secured revenue commitments from enterprises and governments. As of October 29, 2026, Amazon Leo had launched nearly 400 satellites across 14 missions and completed its 1,000th satellite in September 2026. The service will integrate with Amazon Web Services (AWS) for data storage, analytics, and AI. While an anomaly during a ULA Vulcan rocket launch in November 2026 resulted in the loss of 40 satellites, Amazon confirmed this does not affect the timeline for commercial service. The next planned launches include ULA's Leo Vulcan 1 (LV-01) on November 15, 2026 (though an anomaly occurred) and Arianespace's Leo Europe 4 (LE-04) on November 23, 2026. Amazon also signed an agreement in July 2026 to introduce its first satellite internet service in Africa through South African ISP Herotel.

Elon Musk's SpaceX achieved a significant milestone with its Starship program in November 2026, successfully completing its first-ever upper-stage Starship catch. This advancement in reusability is expected to facilitate massive deployments of broadband and AI satellites and future missions to the Moon and Mars.

GraniteShares announced plans on November 17, 2026, to launch two single-stock ETFs linked to Anthropic: the GraniteShares 2x Long Anthropic Daily ETF (NASDAQ: AIL) and the GraniteShares 2x Short Anthropic Daily ETF (NASDAQ: ANS). These are expected to begin trading following Anthropic's public listing, which is targeted for November 19, 2026. Similarly, Leverage Shares by Themes is preparing to launch ANUU (2x long) and Direxion plans to launch ANTO (2x long) and ANTD (2x short), all tied to Anthropic's expected Nasdaq debut around November 19, 2026.

T-REX (REX Shares and Tuttle Capital Management) has also recently launched 2x long ETFs, PURR and ASSX, though specific underlying tickers for these new funds were not explicitly detailed in the provided search results beyond their own ticker. T-REX is known for offering leveraged and inverse single-stock ETFs for companies like Tesla (TSLA), NVIDIA (NVDA), and Apple (AAPL).
